properties.description:
Creating a Requirement, Capability, Component, Decision or Constraint searches the design with the new node's own words. When something close already exists the write is REFUSED and the routes are named — THREE since 2026-09-30, the third being `replaces` (cap:a-capture-can-say-its-node-replaces-an-older-one-and-the-choice-at-the-near-match-check-is-kept): sharpen the existing node by calling the same tool with ITS id (constructors merge, BL-183), or create anyway by passing `distinct_from` with the ids you read and rejected. Interface is report-only, because its parameter struct is shared with other tools and a field there would leak onto all of them.

WHY THE TOOL AND NOT A SKILL. "Search before you add" was already written into FIVE served skills — capture-intent, revise-design, brainstorm, kpp-proposal, retire-from-design — and capture-intent's wording is almost exactly the ask. It still only fired when somebody loaded one. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (accepted) says skill use must be triggered by the situation and "THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER": measured here 2026-07-31, and confirmed from the field 2026-08-11 by a second user whose four-step working path named exactly the two skills he types and neither of the two that would have fired on situations he was already in.

⭐ ANTHONY'S SHARPENING IS WHAT MAKES IT A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A REPORT. The first cut created the node and then listed what looked similar — useless, because by the time the list is read the near-duplicate exists. His words: "there needs to be a deliberate decision of either update already existing node or if it is unique enough, create a new node." So it is the TWO-SIDED ACCEPT (BL-33), the shape `set_artifact_checksum` already uses when it refuses a first baseline and names `baseline_established` as the way through.

HOW THE THRESHOLD AVOIDS THE BM25 TRAP. Scores are not comparable across queries — measured on this design, one topic scored 4.48 and 35.75 for two phrasings — so no absolute cutoff means anything. The node is written FIRST, so it is in the index and ranks for its own text; every other hit is compared to THAT score, inside one query against one corpus. A refusal then rolls the node back. Nothing is compared across queries at any point.

MEASURED CONSERVATIVE, deliberately. During development a moderately-similar pair did NOT clear the bar, and that is the wanted behaviour: a check that refused often would be routed around, and a rule people route around is worse than no rule. The cost is recall — it will miss pairs that are similar but not strongly worded alike.

WHAT IT NEVER DOES: it never merges, never edits, and never refuses a REVISION. Saying the same thing twice in different words is sometimes real signal — `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` exists because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design — so the override is a first-class route rather than an escape hatch.

BULK PATHS ARE UNAFFECTED: genesis, `create_nodes` and `import_graph` do not route through these tools, so seeding many similar nodes at once still works.
properties.name: A capture tool tells you what the design already says, and makes you choose — sharpen or start new
